drug_class: BCR-ABL tyrosine kinase inhibitor (targeted cancer therapy)
purpose: Nilotinib is used to treat a type of blood cancer called chronic myeloid leukemia, or CML. It works best in adults and some children whose cancer is caused by a specific gene abnormality. It helps control the cancer and keep it from getting worse.
how_it_works: Inside your body, an abnormal gene sends signals that tell cancer cells to grow out of control. Nilotinib acts like a lock blocker — it fits into the abnormal protein made by that gene and shuts off the signal. Without that signal, the cancer cells stop growing and eventually die.
common_side_effects: Rash or itchy skin, nausea, headache, tiredness, constipation, muscle or bone pain, and low blood cell counts. You may also notice swelling or a raised rash. Most side effects are manageable, so tell your doctor about anything bothersome.
warnings: This medicine can cause serious heart rhythm problems, including a potentially dangerous irregular heartbeat. It should not be taken with food — you must take it on an empty stomach and wait at least 2 hours before and 1 hour after eating. It can also lower your blood sugar or potassium levels, affect your liver, and interact with many other medications including common antibiotics and antifungals. Tell your doctor about all medicines, vitamins, and herbal supplements you take. Do not take with grapefruit juice.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is 300 mg or 400 mg taken by mouth twice a day, about 12 hours apart, on an empty stomach. Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your condition and how you respond to treatment. Swallow the capsules whole — do not crush or open them.
